rows.name: hud_coin_count (displayed two-digit coin counter)
rows.notes: The two digits drawn in the HUD as "xNN" (tile column 13 tens, 14 ones). Found by differential search with no reference: grabbing the 1-1 ?-block coin twice moved the count 0->1->2, and diff 'increased' (s_coin0->s_coin1, then s_coin1b->s_coin2 with from d1) kept $07EE (1->2) and $07ED among 63 survivors. Proof by write: write_memory $07ED/$07EE = [8,8] did NOT change the screen (the status bar is redrawn only on a coin event), so a real coin was collected; the HUD then showed "x89" and read-back was $07ED=8, $07EE=9. The tens digit appearing as 8 (not the old 0) proves both bytes. Companion per-level binary counter $075E (0-99, used for the 100-coin 1-UP) is separate and RESETS on level restart/game over while these digits persist (after game over $075E read 0 while the HUD still showed x89), so $07ED/$07EE is the persistent displayed coin count. Source: differential search.

rows.name: level_timer (HUD TIME, counts down)
rows.notes: The three digits shown after TIME, counting down from 400 (one per ~24 frames via the $0787 divider; the game's tick helper is $8F5F and the countdown routine $B74F). Found by differential search with no reference: snapshots s_t0->s_t1 with no input (timer 375->356) and s_t1->s_t2 (356->340) narrowed 'changed' survivors from 53 to 26, leaving $07F9 (7->5 then 5->3) and $07FA (5->6 then 6->1); the hundreds byte $07F8 changed only when the hundreds digit rolled. Proof by write: write_memory $07F8-$07FA = [9,9,9] and the HUD immediately showed TIME 999, then ticked itself down to 996 (screenshot) - the written hundreds and tens 9s held, proving all three bytes. Source: differential search.

rows.name: score (HUD MARIO score digits)
rows.notes: Six BCD bytes $07DD-$07E2 = the displayed score divided by 10 (millions..tens of RAM, MSB at $07DD); the ones digit is a fixed '0' tile, so RAM 000040 displays as 000400 and RAM 234587 displays as 2345870. Found by differential search with no reference: grabbing the 1-1 ?-block coin twice (score 000000->000200->000400) left $07E1 as an 'increased' survivor, and read-back of $07DD-$07E2 was [0,0,0,0,4,0]. Extent proof (per the find-variable skill): wrote [1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8] to $07DC-$07E3 and forced a redraw with a coin (which adds 200); the HUD then read "2345870" - the digits of $07DD-$07E2 appeared in order (2,3,4,5,8,7) with $07E1 incremented 6->8 by the +200, while the $07DC '1' and the $07E3 '8' never appeared. That fixes the range at exactly $07DD-$07E2 and shows the coin's +200 lands on $07E1. Source: differential search.

rows.name: coin_count_binary (per-level, 0-99, 100 = 1-UP)
rows.notes: Binary coin counter fed by the coin routine $BBFE (INC $075E) which also grants a 1-UP at 100. Found again by differential search with no reference: the two 1-1 ?-block coins moved it 0->1->2 (survivor $075E in diff d2). It is NOT the displayed value: it resets to 0 on level restart/game over while the persistent HUD digits $07ED/$07EE keep counting (observed $075E=0 with the HUD still reading x89 after game over). Source: differential search.
